description: How to build and govern artificial intelligence that is fair, transparent, private, safe and accountable: the harms AI systems cause, fairness and bias, transparency and explainability, privacy and data rights, safety and robustness, governance and regulation, and what responsible AI means for African contexts. Taught through browser-based exercises that audit real datasets and models for bias, probe them for failures and apply mitigations, grounding each principle in hands-on measurement rather than theory alone.
modelledOn: Barocas, Hardt and Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning
outcomes: Identify and categorise the harms an AI system can cause across its lifecycle.
Measure bias and apply fairness definitions, recognising the trade-offs between them.
Explain model behaviour with interpretability methods and produce transparency documentation.
Protect privacy and uphold data rights when collecting and using data.
Assess and improve the safety and robustness of a model against failures and attacks.
Apply governance frameworks and regulation and adapt responsible-AI practice to African contexts.

units.title: Harms from AI systems
topics: A taxonomy of harms: allocative, representational, quality-of-service, and harms to autonomy and dignity
Where harm enters the lifecycle: problem framing, data, model, deployment and feedback loops
Case studies: biased hiring and credit scoring, flawed facial recognition, content-moderation failures
Harms with regional weight: credit scoring for the unbanked and mobile-money risk models
Stakeholders and the diffusion of responsibility; who bears the cost

units.title: Fairness and bias
topics: Sources of bias: historical, representation, measurement, aggregation and deployment bias
Group fairness definitions: demographic parity, equalised odds, predictive parity
Individual and counterfactual fairness; the impossibility results that force trade-offs
Measuring disparity and auditing a model on a held-out dataset in the browser
Mitigations at pre-processing, in-processing and post-processing stages
Choosing protected attributes sensitively where ethnicity, language and region are involved

units.title: Transparency and explainability
topics: Transparency versus explainability versus interpretability
Intrinsically interpretable models versus post-hoc explanation
Local explanations: feature attribution, LIME and Shapley-value methods
Global explanations, partial-dependence and the limits and misuse of explanations
Documentation: model cards, datasheets for datasets and system fact sheets
Explaining a decision to an affected user such as a declined loan applicant

units.title: Privacy and data rights
topics: Personal data, consent, purpose limitation and data minimisation
Ghana's Data Protection Act 843 and the role of the Data Protection Commission
Re-identification risk and the failure of naive anonymisation
Privacy-preserving techniques: k-anonymity, differential privacy and federated learning in brief
Data collection ethics for low-resource languages and communities; informed consent in practice

units.title: Safety and robustness
topics: Distribution shift and why accuracy on a test set overstates real-world reliability
Adversarial examples and data poisoning; probing a model's brittleness in the browser
Uncertainty estimation, calibration and knowing when to abstain
Robustness to missing data, noisy inputs and intermittent connectivity
Monitoring, drift detection and safe rollback after deployment

units.title: AI governance and regulation
topics: Risk-based governance: the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and an AI management system
The emerging regulatory landscape and risk tiers; sectoral rules for finance and health
Impact assessments, audits and accountability structures within an organisation
Procurement and third-party model risk; responsibility across a supply chain
Standards, voluntary codes and the limits of self-regulation

units.title: AI for African contexts
topics: Data scarcity and representation for African languages, faces and settings
Infrastructure realities: offline and low-bandwidth deployment, on-device models, power cuts
Data sovereignty, benefit sharing and avoiding extractive data practices
Continental and national policy: the African Union's AI stance and local strategy
Building appropriate, locally governed AI rather than importing ill-fitting systems

units.title: A responsible-AI assessment
topics: Combining fairness, transparency, privacy and safety into one evaluation of a system
Producing an impact assessment and a mitigation and monitoring plan
Communicating findings to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Capstone: audit a provided model and dataset and deliver a responsible-AI report with fixes

schedule.title: Harms and the AI lifecycle
schedule.exercise: Pick one AI system you have met in daily life and write a half-page harm map covering who is affected and at which lifecycle stage harm enters.

tasks.title: Classify eight reported harms from AI systems into allocative, representational, quality-of-service and dignity harms and note who was affected
Trace a biased hiring tool case through problem framing, data, model, deployment and feedback, and identify the stage where each harm enters
Investigate a flawed face recognition deployment case, weigh the evidence on errors by group, and decide whether to pause the system, scored by rubric

schedule.title: Regional harms and responsibility
schedule.exercise: Write a stakeholder table for a mobile-money credit scoring model listing each party, what they gain, what they risk and who is answerable.

tasks.title: Review a credit scoring case for the unbanked and list which data features could disadvantage rural women, with evidence for each
Map the stakeholders in a mobile-money risk model case and decide who carries the cost when it wrongly flags a customer
Decide whether to deploy a mobile-money fraud model that blocks some honest traders, weighing harm, benefit and appeal options against a rubric

schedule.title: Bias and fairness metrics
schedule.exercise: Compute demographic parity, equalised odds and predictive parity by hand from a confusion matrix for two groups and compare the three.

tasks.title: Identify the type of bias in each of six case descriptions, such as measurement or representation bias, and cite the evidence in each
Compute group selection rates, true positive rates and precision for a loan dataset and report which fairness definitions the model meets
Show on a given dataset that equal error rates and equal predictive value cannot both hold when base rates differ, and explain what to choose

schedule.title: Auditing a model
schedule.exercise: Write the findings section of an audit memo for a loan model, with the metrics, the groups, the gaps found and the limits of the audit.

tasks.title: Load a held-out loan dataset and compute accuracy for each of three groups to show which group the model serves worse
Test a model by flipping a protected attribute on 200 applicants and count how many decisions change, discussing counterfactual fairness
Audit a model on a held-out dataset with confidence intervals for each group gap, and write which gaps are real and which may be noise

schedule.title: Mitigation and sensitive attributes
schedule.exercise: Describe three mitigation steps at different stages, and say what each trades away in accuracy or simplicity.

tasks.title: Reweight a training set so group sizes balance, retrain, and report the change in accuracy and in the group gap
Apply a post-processing threshold per group to equalise true positive rates, and measure what the change costs in overall accuracy
Decide whether and how to collect ethnicity, language and region data for a fairness audit, balancing audit value against the risk of misuse

schedule.title: Explainability
schedule.exercise: Explain to a classmate the difference between transparency, explainability and interpretability, with one real example of each.

tasks.title: Sort ten statements about a system into transparency, explainability or interpretability claims and note which need more evidence
Train a decision tree and a larger model on the same data, compare their accuracy, and explain which you would use for a high-stakes decision
Compute feature attributions for five predictions with a local method, check them for consistency across similar inputs, and report where they disagree

schedule.title: Documentation and explaining decisions
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page model card for a loan model, covering intended use, data, performance by group, limits and contact for complaints.

tasks.title: Fill in a model card template for a provided model, marking each field that the available evidence cannot support
Draw a partial-dependence plot for two features of a model and identify a misleading pattern that could be produced by correlated inputs
Write the explanation given to a declined loan applicant with the main reasons and next steps, tested against a rubric for clarity and fairness

schedule.title: Data protection and consent
schedule.exercise: List the data a mobile health app collects, and mark which items you would drop under data minimisation and purpose limitation.

tasks.title: Review a consent form for a loan app and mark where it breaks the rules on consent, purpose and minimisation
Decide whether five described data uses are lawful under the Data Protection Act, citing the principle each decision relies on
Re-identify individuals in a released anonymised table by linking it with a public list, and report how many are uniquely identified

schedule.title: Privacy techniques and community data
schedule.exercise: Write a short comparison of k-anonymity, differential privacy and federated learning, with one use and one limit for each.

tasks.title: Generalise a table of ages and districts to reach k-anonymity with k equal to 3, and count the records that lose precision
Add Laplace noise to a count query for several privacy budgets and plot how accuracy changes as the budget tightens
Plan the consented collection of speech data in a local language from a rural community, covering consent, payment and who controls the data, scored by rubric

schedule.title: Robustness and reliability
schedule.exercise: Give three examples of conditions in a rural deployment that differ from the training data and say how each could lower accuracy.

tasks.title: Compare a model's accuracy on a test set and on a shifted set from another region, and report the drop
Create adversarial examples against a small classifier, measure how little change flips its output, and record the success rate
Calibrate a classifier, plot its reliability diagram, and choose an abstain threshold that sends uncertain cases to a human at a set workload

schedule.title: Deployment robustness and monitoring
schedule.exercise: Write a monitoring plan for a deployed model, listing the signals, the thresholds, who is alerted and the rollback steps.

tasks.title: Test a model with 10, 20 and 40 percent of its inputs missing and report how accuracy falls under each fill strategy
Detect a drift in a stream of inputs with a statistical test, and trigger an alert at a stated threshold
Respond to a deployed model that starts failing for one district, deciding evidence needed, rollback timing and communication, scored against a rubric

schedule.title: Governance and regulation
schedule.exercise: Complete a risk register for a hospital triage assistant, scoring likelihood and impact and assigning an owner and control to each risk.

tasks.title: Place a described AI system in the risk-management framework functions and list which activities are missing from its governance
Classify five systems into risk tiers under a regulatory scheme and say which obligations each tier brings
Evaluate a third-party model for a bank, deciding the evidence to request, the contract terms and who is responsible when it fails, scored by rubric

schedule.title: African context and capstone audit
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: audit a provided model and dataset, present fairness, explanation, privacy and robustness results, and recommend fixes with a monitoring plan.

tasks.title: Choose a deployment design for a village clinic with power cuts and poor connectivity, justifying on-device versus cloud with evidence
Produce an impact assessment and a mitigation and monitoring plan for a crop advice app, rated against a rubric
Audit a provided model and dataset for group gaps, privacy leaks and brittleness, apply two fixes and report the before and after results
